subject.title: [Bug] Orphaned/oversized native Codex thread wedges a session permanently — chat.send returns started but no run executes, silently dropping messages

question: For Codex/WebChat sends accepted before native turn execution, should OpenClaw preserve the current immediate ACK contract and add forced rotation plus visible failure telemetry, or change `chat.send` to fail before `started` when the native thread cannot be made runnable?
rationale: Current main has multiple partial mitigations, but the remaining fix is a user-visible liveness contract across ACK timing, native-thread recovery, and audit/health behavior; automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Keep Immediate ACK With Guardrails
options.body: Preserve the documented non-blocking `chat.send` ACK, but add proof-backed forced rotation, error broadcast, and health state so accepted sends cannot vanish silently.

options.title: Fail Before Started
options.body: Delay or preflight enough native-thread work that `chat.send` returns an error instead of `started` when the thread is unrunnable, accepting a compatibility change to ACK timing.

options.title: Wait For Repro Fixture
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides a replayable oversized native-thread fixture or live proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Immediate ACK With Guardrails
recommendation.body: Preserve the documented non-blocking `chat.send` ACK, but add proof-backed forced rotation, error broadcast, and health state so accepted sends cannot vanish silently.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the non-blocking `chat.send` contract and authored adjacent Codex compaction recovery work, so they are the best available owner for the ACK-versus-guardrail product decision.
